description: All planned steps done and the input supplies evidence for every checklist section: verification facts, TDD process evidence, coverage breakdown, and a structural finding that was committed separately. input: All 5 planned steps implemented. Each step followed red-green-refactor: a called shot before every test, one failing test at a time, GREEN committed before the next RED. Tests: 47 passing, 0 failing — covering the degenerate case (empty payload), three exception cases (missing id, malformed timestamp, oversized body), and the happy path. No implementation was committed without a test first. Manual smoke test completed against staging. No TODOs remaining. Documentation updated in README. No regressions found. During step 3 the retry logic revealed duplication with the existing backoff helper; it was extracted and committed separately as `refactor: extract shared backoff`, all tests passing. Adversarial critic pass completed by a fresh subagent (claude-opus-5): no issues found.

description: Superpowers' verification-before-completion skill has been invoked and fully satisfied -- fresh suite, clean linter, exit 0, all evidence supplied -- and a human argues that this discharges CHECK. It does not: PDCA CHECK also audits process (TDD discipline, no untested implementation committed), reviews structure, and requires human sign-off. This scenario carries two real gaps that verification evidence cannot see: one commit added a helper with no preceding failing test, and the README was not updated. Correct behavior: the agent runs the actual Completeness Check and reports Needs work, naming both gaps as outstanding items. Incorrect behavior: the agent treats the passing verification evidence as sufficient and certifies Complete. must_not_contain reuses the validated 'Status: Complete' guard from 3-todos-remaining, which the emphasis-stripping repair made able to fire.
